expected_answer.root_cause: The Tempo distributor uses dskit shuffle-sharding to choose ingester replicas per trace ID, and the dskit ring/ring.go::IsHealthy gate is consulted to decide which ring members are eligible. When a peer ingester becomes unresponsive but its heartbeat in ring/lifecycler.go is still inside the unhealthy-timeout window, IsHealthy returns true for that peer and the shuffle-shard set degenerates: every trace ID hashes onto the same surviving ingester. That ingester's modules/ingester/instance.go::CutCompleteTraces cannot keep up because modules/ingester/flush.go::handleFlush is contending on the global block-builder lock, so live traces accumulate to the 3M cap while peers stay flat. Back-pressure does not trip because the distributor keeps selecting the saturated ingester until heartbeats finally time out and the unhealthy peer is evicted.
error_chain: Distributor receives a trace and computes a shuffle-shard over the dskit ring
dskit ring/ring.go::IsHealthy returns true for the stale (but not yet timed-out) peer in ring/lifecycler.go

Shuffle-shard set degenerates because the unhealthy peer occupies a slot but is unreachable, so the distributor's replication path repeatedly falls back to the same surviving ingester for every trace ID
All inbound traces land on the same hot ingester (ingester-7)
The hot ingester's modules/ingester/instance.go::CutCompleteTraces falls behind moving completed traces out of the live set
modules/ingester/flush.go::handleFlush contends on the global block-builder lock, increasing lock_wait_ms and queue length
Live traces accumulate from ~250K to the 3M cap on the hot ingester while peers remain at ~250K
Back-pressure never trips because the distributor keeps picking the same hot ingester until the unhealthy peer's heartbeat finally times out
affected_components: Tempo distributor (modules/distributor) — consults the ring for shuffle-shard membership
Tempo ingester (modules/ingester/instance.go, modules/ingester/flush.go) — saturates on the funneled load
dskit ring (ring/ring.go, ring/lifecycler.go) — health/heartbeat semantics that drive shard selection
All trace ingestion during the heartbeat-timeout window for an unresponsive peer
expected_answer.remediation: Three layered options: (1) Tighten ring/ring.go::IsHealthy (or its callers in shuffle-shard) to exclude peers whose heartbeat is older than a configurable threshold below the full unhealthy timeout, so degenerate shard sets are avoided. (2) Make shuffle-shard saturation-aware: have the distributor consult per-ingester live-trace headroom and rotate off saturated members. (3) Reduce block-builder lock contention in modules/ingester/flush.go::handleFlush so the ingester can drain its live trace set fast enough that the funneled load doesn't reach the 3M cap. The structural fix lives in dskit; the throughput fix lives in Tempo's flush path.
